evidence: root-vm.postgres completed the PostgreSQL create, insert, select, restart, and select script
claims.adjudication: The raw run was marked failed only because Azure Run Command returned no stdout to an outer string-count assertion. The guest command itself succeeded and used psql ON_ERROR_STOP.

evidence: data-vm.postgres-write passed with an in-guest SQL value assertion
the first VM was deleted before the retained disk was attached to the replacement VM
replacement-vm.postgres-read passed with the same in-guest SQL value assertion

combinedDecision: an additional data disk is not required for PostgreSQL startup; a retained Azure data disk is one confirmed realization of storage that survives VM replacement
limitations: Every Azure VM still has an OS disk; diskless VM is not the tested condition.
This is one development observation in one provider and region.
Other CSPs and retained boot-disk policies require their own provider-specific interpretation.
The result does not establish high availability, backup, replication, or disk performance.
